sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:1
items.html: These vessels of Akudim are the first vessels: That is, the vessels of the first expansion, from which the aforementioned male and female of Keter rose. (See above, Part 4, Chapter 1, item 5, in the words of the ARI and in the Inner Light.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:2
items.html: The upper light would be drawn downward, etc., the vessels would be nullified: That is to say, had the level of Keter expanded back into the vessels as it was at first, before its departure, then the vessels that were made at the time of the departure would have returned and been nullified, for the reason the ARI wrote above, Part 4, Chapter 6, item 3; see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:3
items.html: It was necessary that the lights of the ZON in the vessel of Keter rise upward by themselves, for since these ZON of Keter, which rose upward by means of the screen that was refined, have only the coarseness of phase three — as above in the adjacent passage beginning “The male,” see there — therefore they draw only the level of Hochma, and the light of Hochma clothes in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, and so forth. And it follows that every vessel lacks much of the measure of light that befits it, for the vessel of Keter now has only the light of Hochma, which is far lower than it; and likewise the vessel of Hochma has only the light of Bina, and so forth. And because of this the coarseness in the vessels became recognisable, in such a way that they could not be nullified.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:4
items.html:
6) “It does not reach Keter” is because the ZON of Keter rise upward: That is to say, the matter of the departure of the level of Keter of the first expansion, which is called “it does not reach Keter,” is the matter of the departure of the ZON of Keter upward — that is, that they are found rising there, to be included in the upper coupling that is in the Malchut of the Rosh [head]. And this matter has already been explained at length in Part 4, Inner Light, Chapter 4, item 50, and from there you shall seek it. I will bring here only the essence, and in brief, enough to explain the words of the ARI here. And behold, it was explained there that the whole principal cause of the departure of the lights from the first expansion of Akudim was only by reason of the ascent of Malchut alone, the meaning of which is the refinement of the screen in the vessel of Malchut: for when Malchut rose to ZA, which is phase three, the level of Keter vanished; and afterward, when it rose from ZA to Bina, the level of Hochma likewise vanished; and afterward, when it rose from Bina to Hochma, the level of Bina vanished; and when it rose from Hochma to Keter, the level of ZA vanished too; and afterward, when it rose from the vessel of Keter to the Emanator, that is, to the Malchut of the Rosh, the whole of the light of that expansion vanished. And behold, all these lights that departed from there left records behind them in their vessels — except for Malchut, that is, phase four, which left no record behind it after its departure. It was also explained there that Malchut — that is, the screen in her — at the time when it is refined and rises from phase to phase, is found to be included in the records that the lights left behind them in those phases. For when the screen is refined from phase four to phase three, which is the vessel of ZA, it is included in the record that remained there from the light of ZA after its departure; and likewise afterward, when it rose and was refined to phase two, which is the vessel of Bina, it is found included also in the record that remained there from the light of Bina after its departure; and likewise when it rose to Hochma it was included in the record of Hochma; and when it rose to Keter it was included in the record of Keter. In such a way that in its ascent afterward from Keter to the Emanator, the screen is found included of all the records that are in the ten Sefirot of the first expansion, except for the record of phase four, it having vanished even from the Malchut of the first expansion herself, as above.
And know that the principal of those records included in the screen are the coarseness of phase three, which remained from the level of Hochma, and the coarseness of phase four in the aspect of clothing, which remained from the level of Keter; for the records of the levels that are lower than them are included in the upper records mentioned.
And know that although the level of Keter rises immeasurably above the level of Hochma, these two records can nevertheless both be one degree here, differing only as male and female. And this is for the reason that the record of the level of Keter is only half a record — and moreover, it is the more important half that it lacks. For it has already been brought above that every record is discerned in two: a record of drawing and a record of clothing. This means that the greatness of a level is measured by the measure of the coarseness in the screen, in which the coarser draws a higher level; however, since the higher level needs the more refined vessel, it comes out that we discern in every level two opposite extremes, valued one against the other. For just as the greatest level is obliged, from one extreme, to have the coarsest screen and vessel of Malchut, which are the vessels of drawing for the great level, so from its other extreme it is obliged to have the most refined vessels of reception, which will suit the clothing of the greatest light.
And therefore those records that remained from the first expansion are each discerned in the two halves mentioned, that is, a record of drawing and a record of clothing. And know that the record of drawing is the principal one, for the upper coupling is made upon it, and from it rises the reflected light that connects and clothes the upper light in the Partzuf.
And with what has been explained you will well understand why the record of the level of Keter and the record of the level of Hochma are considered male and Nukva — which seems very puzzling, for it is known that male and female must be in equivalence with one another, since otherwise how would they have contact with one another, and how would they bestow upon and receive from one another? And here the male is from the level of Keter and the female from the level of Hochma, whose superiority of Keter over Hochma is immeasurable, as is known. But with what has been explained — that the record of the level of Keter is only half of that record, and moreover its weaker half, since it is not fit for the drawing of the light by its own side alone, whereas the record of phase three is a complete record, both in the aspect of drawing and in the aspect of clothing — it follows that the complete record of phase three is equivalent with half the record of the level of Keter. Understand this, and remember it well for all that follows here.
And below it will be explained how this male and female join with the screen in the Malchut of the Rosh in a single coupling, by reason of their ascent there, whereby they return and once more draw an expansion of the upper light to the Partzuf, which is called the second expansion. And this is what he says, “when it does not reach Keter, it is because the male and female of Keter rise upward, etc., and then the root of the upper Keter bestows downward.” Which is as written above: that at the time when it does not reach Keter — that is, in the first expansion, which as a whole is called Keter — then there are found rising from this level of Keter the aspects of male and female, the male being the aspect of the record of Keter of that level of Keter, and the female being the aspect of the record of Hochma of that same level of Keter; and they rise beneath the Malchut of the Rosh and are renewed there in a new coupling, as he goes on to explain.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:5
items.html:
They remain in its place, etc., the root of Malchut rises into the root of Yesod: And you must know here this rule, that the ascent of the branches — the meaning of which is the refinement of the coarseness in them — causes also the ascent of their roots. And although refinement does not apply in the roots, which are the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head], nevertheless the ascent of the roots follows from the refinement in the branches themselves; for the relation of the branches to their roots is as the relation of “the actual to the potential,” and they are in truth one essence, and there is nothing in the actual but what is in the potential. Therefore, if there is some revelation to the branches, which are the Sefirot of the Guf [body], that revelation is obliged to appear first in the ten Sefirot of the roots. And therefore, though it is true that this matter of the refinement and departure of lights from the aspect of their clothing in vessels cannot occur in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh — since the whole clothing of the lights in vessels is not there except in potential — the matter of the raising of the place of the coupling certainly is there, only that this comes about by reason of the ascent of the branches there.
And this knowledge is among the most important in this wisdom, and further on the ARI expands this matter into all its particulars; here he speaks only in general terms. And he says that the ascent of the ZON of the level of Keter of the Guf to beneath the Malchut of the Rosh causes the light of Keter to be included in the aspect of the vessel of the Malchut of the Rosh. And these two inclusions — the inclusion of the ZON of Keter of the Guf beneath the Malchut of the Rosh in the place of the light of Keter of the Guf, and the inclusion of the light of Keter of the Guf in the vessel of Malchut herself — cause the root of Malchut, the meaning of which is the screen included in the vessel of Malchut of the Rosh, to rise to the place of the root of Yesod, that is, to the aspect of the coarseness of phase three, as is written at length.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:6
items.html: The root of the upper Keter bestows downward, that is, an abundant bestowal by way of a coupling in order to beget offspring, which are the ten Sefirot of the second expansion, called Partzuf AB of AK, which is regarded as an offspring and a son to the first Partzuf of AK.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:7
items.html: A preparation for the lower ones to receive, that is, the correction of the screen, in such a way that it will be fit and ready to couple with the upper light. As written further on.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:5:8
items.html: The Nukva of Keter is included in the male, meaning that this coupling is not made upon the record of phase three, which is the aspect of the female, as above, but is made upon the aspect of the record of phase four, which is the aspect of the male of Keter. But the female is included with him in the illumination of the coupling, as will be explained before us.
